slide_text: Logarithms Logarithms sound intimidating, but you already understand them. You ll prove it to yourself in the next few minutes starting with nothing more than counting zeros. Navigate: press or Space to advance | to go back
Part 1: Counting Zeros
Look at these numbers: Number How many zeros? 10 100 1000 10000

fragments.text: ? 1 How many zeros does 10 have? That s right! 10 has 1 zero. How many zeros does 100 have?
? 2 That s right! 100 has 2 zeros. How many zeros does 1000 have?
? 3 That s right! 1000 has 3 zeros. How many zeros does 10000 have?
? 4 That s right! 10000 has 4 zeros. Do you see the pattern? Each time we add a zero, the count goes up by 1. How many zeros does 100000 have?
? 5 That s right! 100000 has 5 zeros. This number of zeros has a fancy name: logarithm .

slide_text: In Python, is the power operator. means 10 to the power of 2 . What does each expression give? Expression Value Log

fragments.text: The power tells you how many zeros. The number of zeros tells you the power. Going from power number is exponentiation . Going from number power is logarithm .

slide_text: So when someone asks what is log(1000)? they are really asking: 10 to the power of what gives 1000? What is the answer?

fragments.text: That s right! The answer is 3 , because 10 10 10 = 10 3 = 1000.
That s it. That s all a logarithm is. Let s fill out a few more: Question In other words Answer log(10) 10 ? = 10 ? 1 log(100) 10 ? = 100 ? 2 log(1000) 10 ? = 1000 ? 3 log(10000) 10 ? = 10000 ? 4

slide_text: Part 2: The Power Question
Quick fire: answer without Python.

fragments.text: 10 to the power of what gives 100? Think: how many times do you multiply 10 by itself to get 100? That s right! 2 , because 10 10 = 10 2 = 100. 10 to the power of what gives 10?
That s right! 1 , because 10 1 is just 10 itself. 10 to the power of what gives 1? (Tricky! What happens when the power is 0?)
That s right! 0 , because any number to the power of 0 is 1. Try in Python you get 1. So what is log(1)?
That s right! log(1) = 0 . Key fact: log of 1 is always 0 , no matter what the base is. Because anything 0 = 1.

slide_text: What is log(500)? In other words: 10 to the power of what gives 500? It s not a whole number. But you already know something about it.

fragments.text: 10 2 = 100 too small 10 3 = 1000 too big So log(500) is between 2 and 3 . Just take a guess!

slide_text: Part 6: Beyond Base 10 Up to now, every log you computed was secretly log base 10 counting zeros only works because our number system is built on powers of 10. From here on we ll write the base explicitly, like log 2 or log 3 , because the base is about to change.
